items.title: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
items.excerpt: This technical deep dive examines EvilTokens, a sophisticated framework enabling persistent device-code phishing attacks that bypass MFA and conditional access controls. Attackers harvest long-lived tokens by tricking users into authorizing malicious apps, granting them seamless access to M365 and Azure resources. Infrastructure teams must audit OAuth app permissions, revoke suspicious device codes, and implement token lifetime restrictions to neutralize this identity takeover vector.

items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign | Microsoft Security Blog
items.excerpt: Threat actors are integrating generative AI to automate device-code phishing campaigns, dynamically generating realistic login pages and contextual lures that adapt to victim behavior. The AI-driven infrastructure scales attacks rapidly while evading signature-based detection. Defenders should deploy AI-aware web filtering, monitor for anomalous OAuth consent requests, and enforce strict conditional access rules to block automated identity harvesting attempts.

items.title: Device Code Phishing is an Evolution in Identity Takeover | Proofpoint US
items.excerpt: Device code phishing has emerged as a primary vector for identity takeover, allowing attackers to bypass traditional password and MFA defenses by exploiting OAuth 2.0 authorization flows. This analysis outlines the attack lifecycle, detection signatures, and mitigation strategies for enterprise environments. IT infrastructure teams must prioritize monitoring of device code endpoints, implement just-in-time access controls, and educate users on recognizing authorization prompts.

items.title: Access granted: phishing with device code authorization for account takeover | Proofpoint US
items.excerpt: This foundational report details how attackers leverage device code authorization flows to harvest valid access tokens, effectively bypassing multi-factor authentication. By directing users to malicious consent pages, threat actors gain persistent access to cloud identities. Defenders should audit Azure AD sign-in logs for device code flows, restrict third-party app registrations, and deploy identity protection solutions to detect and block anomalous authorization requests.
